summary:
XYNTHORA LUNAR is an interactive lunar mission planning prototype designed to help users compare candidate landing sites near the Moon's south pole.

Using NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data, the application visualizes solar elevation, Earth visibility, and changes in mission conditions across different dates and locations.

Built with Python, Flask, and React, XYNTHORA combines interactive landing-site comparison, mission delay simulation, visibility timelines, and downloadable scientific reports into an accessible dashboard.

The project aims to make complex lunar mission planning data easier to understand for engineers, researchers, educators, and the public. The current prototype provides preliminary geometric analysis, while terrain-aware visibility calculations remain under development.
details:
The Problem

Lunar south pole missions face extreme lighting conditions and limited direct-to-Earth communication opportunities. Evaluating alternative landing locations and schedules requires interpreting complex astronomical data.

Our Solution

XYNTHORA LUNAR is a web-based mission planning and decision-support platform that simplifies lunar landing-site analysis.

Implemented Prototype Features

  • NASA Ephemeris Integration: Retrieves Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation data using NASA JPL Horizons.
  • Landing Site Comparison: Compares astronomical conditions at two candidate locations.
  • Interactive Visualization: Displays sampled Sun and Earth positions through charts.
  • Visibility Timeline: Shows sampled periods of geometric Sun and Earth visibility.
  • Mission Rescue Mode: Provides a prototype for comparing original and delayed mission dates.
  • Lunar Surface Explorer: Provides a map-based interface for choosing candidate coordinates.

Additional Modules Under Development

  • Terrain elevation visualization using NASA LOLA data.
  • Local horizon obstruction calculations.
  • Mission decision scoring based on user-defined priorities.
  • CSV and JSON scientific report generation.

Technology Stack

Frontend: React, JavaScript, Recharts, Leaflet, CSS.

Backend: Python, Flask, NumPy, Requests.

Scientific resources: NASA JPL Horizons, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data, and Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA).

Scientific Limitations

The verified ephemeris calculations use a geometric horizon model. Local topographic obstructions, accurate power generation, continuous communication windows, and landing safety have not yet been fully validated.

XYNTHORA is an educational and preliminary mission-screening prototype, not a flight-certified mission planning system.

Impact

XYNTHORA demonstrates how open NASA data can be transformed into an intuitive decision-support experience, making lunar exploration planning more accessible and improving understanding of the engineering constraints of south polar missions.
